bug_semantics: When the experimental built-in HTTP API is enabled, its unauthenticated Express routes accept requests solely because the TCP listener is bound to 127.0.0.1; they do not validate the HTTP Host or Origin. Malicious web content can therefore reach the loopback service through a browser/CSRF path or DNS rebinding and invoke API endpoints under an attacker-controlled or cross-origin host. The advisory classifies this as SSRF with low confidentiality impact and cites NTLM behavior; the repository's fix and tests explicitly identify the two concrete trust-boundary failures as DNS rebinding and browser-origin requests.
flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the initial first-party HTTP API implementation: commit a3cbce61901651d526d9575f3c4bb2aafc21c40f created public/httpServer.js with an unauthenticated action route and a loopback-only listener but no Host or Origin validation. The later TypeScript migration preserved that behavior and is not the BIC.

The vulnerable lifecycle starts immediately after the 3.57.0 release commit. a3cbce61901651d526d9575f3c4bb2aafc21c40f is the smallest causal commit because it first creates the HTTP server, exposes API action execution, and treats loopback binding as the security boundary; its direct parent has no public/httpServer.js at all. The later f67761903935d35fd85609cfb5c6f016a8f431c6 TypeScript migration only carries the mechanism to src/main/httpServer.ts, so attributing that move would violate the BIC rule. The BIC is included in v3.58.0 and persists through the advisory's last affected release, v3.69.0. Direct fix 260802348955231442c4bae6c2d9d8ede947af0a adds the missing application-layer boundary: exact loopback Host validation defeats DNS rebinding, and rejection of any Origin prevents a web browser from driving the API. Although no separately versioned fixed release has been published, the repository has a concrete direct source fix. Finally, the complete BIC commit object is human-authored/committed by Mikael Finstad and contains no AI attribution trailer or bot identity.
